reviewer: book-publication-reviewer v1.0 (manual run, 2026-07-19; PR-2 resolution pass 2026-07-19)

findings.summary: The deterministic evidence flagged both names as 'explained late' (used p80, explained p90). Reading page 80 directly: the book names both characters explicitly and immediately — 'Now let me name them for you... The boy's name was Salih, and his father's name was al-Bakhtari.' This is a full introduction on the page of first use, not a gap. The evidence tool's explanation-detection heuristic did not recognize the 'X's name was Y' construction and matched a later, unrelated page instead. Fixed at the tool level (scripts/podcast/_book_comprehension.py: added a short backward-looking window for name-reveal cues) rather than by writing an unnecessary bridge. Re-running the evidence after the fix reports 0 prerequisite gaps for this book.

Asif's decision: Sharia is the book's standard spelling. On resolution, direct literal search of book.md found the original review undercounted the drift: TWO non-standard spellings existed, not one — 'Shari'ah' in the augment editorial note (line 103) AND, separately, 'Shari'a' inside the base narrative translation itself (line 334, in the boy's dialogue on cosmology), which the first pass's page-32 reading did not surface. Root cause traced one level deeper than the augment prompt: _system/glossary.yml carried TWO entries for the same underlying term (الشريعة/sharīʿa) — 'Sharia' and 'Shariʿa' — because nothing in the glossary bake step deduplicates by underlying root. Fix applied: both book.md occurrences corrected to 'Sharia'; the duplicate glossary entry removed, leaving one canonical entry; book.pdf re-rendered; comprehension evidence re-run clean (0 prerequisite gaps, matching the corrected single spelling). Literal search of the re-rendered PDF confirms 6 occurrences of 'Sharia', 0 of any other spelling. NOT bridge-fixed — bridges add orientation, not spelling corrections — the book text itself and its glossary were corrected directly, with Asif's explicit authorization.

notes: Two P1/P2 items on the evidence surfaced on first pass; both required direct reading of the PDF (not the evidence alone) to judge correctly, exactly as the reviewer contract requires.

PR-1 turned out not to be a reader-facing defect at all -- the fix applied was to the checker's own explanation-detection heuristic (a real, generalizable improvement now covered by tests), not a bridge to the book. No bridge was written or needed.

PR-2 was real, and the first pass's count (1 occurrence) was itself incomplete -- a second drifted spelling existed outside the page the first pass read closely. Resolved by direct book.md + glossary.yml correction after Asif chose 'Sharia' as the standard, not by a bridge.

naming_drift() has a known scope limit: it can only detect drift between spellings that both appear as distinct glossary entries, and even then only via literal string search, not fuzzy/apostrophe-insensitive matching. This instance's root cause -- a duplicate glossary entry for one term -- was found and fixed for THIS book, but the detector's general blind spot (apostrophe/diacritic-insensitive drift, spellings with no glossary entry at all) remains open for other books. Tracked on the pipeline backlog as naming-drift-scope-limit -- deliberately NOT built out into a general canonicalization system in this pass, since that is more infrastructure than a single-word content decision warrants.
